subject: DPA negotiation: data lifecycle & archive sunset language
messages:
From: John Miller <jmiller@trustcorp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@trustcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Initial DPA questions: lifecycle, archive sunset, backups

Connor —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our vendor security review surfaced a couple of DPA items we want clarified before Legal signs off. I attached the questionnaire. High-level items we need answers on:

- Exact retention windows for (a) primary production data, (b) backups/snapshots, and (c) archival copies; is there a guaranteed maximum for any of these?
- Process and timing for confirmed deletion requests (erasures) from customers; do you provide attestations/certificates?
- If we request onshore-only processing for EU accounts, can you commit to EU-only data flow and prevent cross-border fallthroughs for logs/metrics?
- Any circumstances where data may be retained for legal hold / investigation and how that interacts with your SLA

Attachment: TrustCorp_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (pdf)

Can you get back with a concise proposed DPA clause set we can take to Legal? If you prefer a call, happy to schedule.

Thanks,
John Miller
Head of Vendor Security
TrustCorp Financial

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: John Miller <jmiller@trustcorp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Jul 2028 11:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions: lifecycle, archive sunset, backups

John —

Appreciate the detail. Attaching a short audit summary and high-level answers below; Stephanie (Security & Compliance) is looped in and will propose redline language. Happy to do a 30-minute call if you want to walk through specifics.

High-level responses:
- Primary production: customer data retained as long as the account is active; on termination we initiate erasure workflows (see below).
- Backups/snapshots: rolling snapshots retained up to 30 days for recovery; snap-level snapshots are immutable but scheduled deletion occurs thereafter.
- Archive/Sunset: for customers who opt into archival export we retain exported archives for up to 180 days unless otherwise requested.
- Deletion/Erasures: standard confirmation provided within 90 days of a verified erasure request; we can offer an accelerated timeline under enterprise agreements. We provide deletion attestations as a standard artifact.
- EU-only processing: our EU Private deployment supports EU-only data flow; logs and metrics can be configured to avoid cross-border export.
- Legal hold: we will preserve data for the duration of a valid legal hold and will notify the customer; retention extends only as required.

Attachment: Redwood_Audit_Summary.pdf (pdf)

Proposed next step: Stephanie will suggest redline language for the DPA retention/deletion clauses this afternoon.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Jul 2028 12:40:00 +0100
Subject: Draft redline wording for retention / deletion / residency (internal)

Connor / Aditya —

Quick draft language to propose to TrustCorp Legal. Keep it tight and negotiable; I flagged the bits I think we should hold firm on.

1) Retention windows (production / backups / archive) — draft: 
"Customer Data: Redwood will retain Customer Data for the duration of the customer's active subscription. After termination, Redwood will initiate deletion of Customer Data within thirty (30) days and will complete deletion from primary stores within ninety (90) days. Immutable backups and snapshots are retained for disaster recovery for up to thirty (30) days; any archival exports created at the customer's request will be retained for up to one hundred eighty (180) days unless Customer requests earlier deletion."

Notes: push back on mandatory <30-day deletion completion unless compensated; we can offer 30-day for primary overwrite but complete removal from backups is operationally 90 days.

2) Deletion attestations — draft: 
"Upon completion of deletion, Redwood will provide a deletion attestation certifying that Customer Data has been removed from active production systems and that deletion workflows for immutable backups have been initiated. Redwood may use technical means (cryptographic tombstoning / key destruction) for rapid logical deletion where available and will document the approach in the attestation."

Notes: we should avoid promising third-party certified deletion by default; offer as paid add-on or add to SOC/audit deliverable.

3) Residency / onshore processing — draft: 
"Residency: Upon Customer's election of an EU-only deployment option, Redwood will process and store Customer Data within the EU region and will not intentionally transfer such Customer Data outside the EU, except where required by law. Logs and operational telemetry that include Customer Data identifiers will be stored in-region; aggregated, non-identifying telemetry may be used for platform health and may be processed outside the region."

Notes: this language gives us room for aggregated telemetry processing outside region — TrustCorp may push.

If you want, I'll package these into a single tracked-change redline (proposed_dpa_redline.txt) and we can send to John.

-Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference

Deletion attestations: Upon completion of deletion, Redwood will provide a deletion attestation certifying that Customer Data has been removed from active production systems and that deletion workflows for immutable backups have been initiated. From: John Miller <jmiller@trustcorp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@trustcorp.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 15:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft redline wording for retention / deletion / residency

Connor —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear wording. A few items from our side:

1) Deletion / SLA — TrustCorp requires confirmation of completion within 30 days of an erasure request for consumer data; for enterprise accounts we are willing to accept 60 days but 90 is our maximum for backups. Can Redwood move to a 60-day completion timeline for enterprise customers and 30 days for consumer-facing accounts?

2) Backups — we need stronger language about backups being encrypted at rest and the mechanism for deletion (you mentioned key destruction / tombstoning). Please add: "Backups are encrypted using customer-segregated keys and Redwood will securely destroy corresponding keys to render backups unreadable as a method of deletion when applicable."

3) Attestation — acceptable, but we need more detail: the attestation must include timestamped logs of deletion events and the identities of internal operators who executed the workflow.

4) Residency — appreciate the in-region option. Legal will push for explicit language preventing transfer of logs/telemetry that contain any Customer Data identifiers outside the EU unless pseudonymized to industry-standard techniques. Aggregated, non-identifying metrics are OK to process outside region.

Let's do a 30-minute call tomorrow morning (10:00 CET) to finalize. If you can update the redline with the three bullets above before the call, Legal will be able to greenlight faster.

Regards,
John Miller
Head of Vendor Security
TrustCorp Financial
